papers.title: Do Sentence Interactions Matter? Leveraging Sentence Level Representations for Fake News Classification

generated_questions.question: How are documents represented as graphs in the proposed model?
generated_questions.answer: Each document is represented as a graph where nodes correspond to sentences and edges represent the semantic similarity between pairs of sentences.

generated_questions.question: What method is used to initialize the edge scores in the document graph?
generated_questions.answer: Edge scores are initialized using BERT fine-tuned on the semantic textual similarity (SS) task.

generated_questions.question: What is the dimensionality of the randomly initialized word embeddings used in the model?
generated_questions.answer: 100 dimensions.

generated_questions.question: Which pooling method is used after the graph neural network layers?
generated_questions.answer: Max-pooling is used for pooling node representations.

generated_questions.question: What kind of activation function and its specific parameter is used in GCN and GAT models?
generated_questions.answer: LeakyReLU activation function with a slope of 0.2.

generated_questions.question: How are sentence embeddings obtained before being passed to the graph neural network?
generated_questions.answer: Sentence embeddings are obtained using the last hidden state of a single-layer LSTM applied to the words of the sentence.

generated_questions.question: Which datasets are used for the four-way classification experiment?
generated_questions.answer: LUN-train (split 80:20 for training and dev) and LUN-test (as out of domain test set).

generated_questions.question: How is the SLN dataset used in the experiments?
generated_questions.answer: SLN is used as an out-of-domain test set for two-way classification between satire and trusted articles and is not used for training.

generated_questions.question: What strategy is used for the pooling of node representations before the final classification layer?
generated_questions.answer: Max-pool is used for pooling node embeddings before the fully connected projection layer.

generated_questions.question: How does the attention map differ between satirical and trusted news articles according to the qualitative analysis?
generated_questions.answer: Trusted news articles' attention maps focus on two specific sentences, while satirical articles have more distributed attention across sentences.

generated_questions.question: What is the main reason for not experimenting with the semantic similarity (SS) model for GCN in the four-way classification scenario?
generated_questions.answer: The semantic similarity model does not have much impact on GCN performance and is computationally expensive.

generated_questions.question: What type of macro-averaging is used for reporting scores?
generated_questions.answer: Macro-averaged scores are reported for all experimental settings.

generated_questions.question: What future research direction is suggested based on the attention map findings?
generated_questions.answer: Understanding the differences in sentence interaction patterns in different types of articles for deeper text analysis.

generated_questions.question: What methodology was used to resolve annotation disagreements in the dataset?
generated_questions.answer: Labels with 100% agreement were accepted; for majority agreement above 66%, those were selected; for complete disagreement, one of the authors and two extra human judges reviewed the tweets to achieve majority agreement above 66%.

generated_questions.question: What preprocessing steps were applied to the tweets before annotation?
generated_questions.answer: URLs, emojis, emoticons were removed, usernames and user mentions were replaced by '@USER', duplicate punctuation was normalized, and duplicate tweets were removed.

generated_questions.question: Which features were tested for classical machine learning models?
generated_questions.answer: TF/IDF unigrams, bigrams, POS tags, and dependency relation tags were tested as features.

generated_questions.question: What threshold was used for ignoring terms appearing too frequently in the documents during feature selection?
generated_questions.answer: Terms appearing in more than 80% of the documents were ignored.

generated_questions.question: What embedding dimensions were used for Greek word embeddings in the deep learning models?
generated_questions.answer: Greek word embeddings with 300 dimensions were used.

generated_questions.question: Which BERT model was used for the deep learning experiments, and why?
generated_questions.answer: The multilingual BERT cased model trained on 108 languages was used, as there was no monolingual Greek BERT model available.

generated_questions.question: What were the settings for the penalty parameter C and gamma in the SVM classifiers?
generated_questions.answer: The value of C was set to 1 for both SVMs; gamma for the RBF SVM was set to 2.

generated_questions.question: How was accentuation in Greek text handled during preprocessing?
generated_questions.answer: All words were lower-cased and normalized to their non-accented equivalent to address inconsistencies in accent usage.

generated_questions.question: Which machine learning model achieved the best recall score for the Offensive class among classical models?
generated_questions.answer: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) classifier yielded the best recall score for the Offensive class, at 0.61.

generated_questions.question: How did the addition of POS and dependency relation tags affect classical model performance?
generated_questions.answer: Adding POS and dependency relation tags marginally improved the Linear SVM's recall for the Offensive class, but generally decreased performance for other classifiers.

generated_questions.question: Which classical machine learning model performed best overall on OGTD?
generated_questions.answer: Linear SVM performed best overall among classical machine learning models, with a macro-F1 of 0.80.

generated_questions.question: What was the effect of using TF/IDF bigram features compared to unigram features?
generated_questions.answer: Models trained with TF/IDF bigram features performed worse on all evaluation metrics compared to unigrams, except for Multinomial Naïve Bayes which improved in F1-score for the Not Offensive class.

generated_questions.question: How was the spaCy pipeline used in feature extraction?
generated_questions.answer: The spaCy pipeline for Greek was used to extract POS-tags and dependency relations for every token in a tweet, which were then transformed to count matrices.

generated_questions.question: What limitation regarding sentiment lexicons for Greek is mentioned?
generated_questions.answer: A suitable sentiment lexicon for Greek was not available and thus could not be used in the experiments.

generated_questions.question: What was the macro F1-score achieved by the best deep learning model?
generated_questions.answer: The best deep learning model (LSTM and GRU with Attention) achieved a macro F1-score of 0.89.

generated_questions.question: What was the observed performance of the multilingual BERT model compared to monolingual Greek embeddings?
generated_questions.answer: The fine-tuned BERT-Base Multilingual Cased model did not achieve good results; monolingual Greek word embeddings performed significantly better.

generated_questions.question: What future work or limitations did the authors mention regarding linguistic features?
generated_questions.answer: It is not clear whether the limited improvement from linguistic features is due to the accuracy of the Greek spaCy model or the features themselves; improving spaCy or other Greek NLP tools could be future work.

generated_questions.answer: OGTD v2.0 was created by collecting and annotating an additional 5,508 tweets in November 2019; the new dataset totals 10,287 instances.
